text:
Marta (Support): AcmeApp escalated — intermittent 5xx / 504 gateway timeouts during a midday burst (around 12:10-12:20 PST). They see upstream read timeouts and customer retries. Sample: `{"status":504, "id":"req_abc123", "msg":"upstream read timeout"}`

Izzy (oncall): Thanks — can you paste a sample request_id + which model/route they're hitting? Any correlation with tenant or region?

Marta (Support): route: `/v1/generate`, model: `redwood-open-7b`, tenant: `acme-prod`. Customer provided repro: many parallel calls (burst) -> first ~10 succeed then bursts start seeing 504 after ~30s. Example curl: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"redwood-open-7b","input":"..."}'```

Ravi (SRE): I'm pulling infra metrics now. I can see KEDA ScaledObject pulses at that time and the controller attempts scale 0->4. However pods are staying NotReady for ~35-45s due to model init/warm. HPA minReplicas is 0 for this tenant and readiness probe initialDelay is 30s — combined this means traffic is hitting gateway while pods still unready. KEDA pollingInterval is 30s which causes delayed scale reactions.

Ravi (SRE): Found ScaledObject snippet in prod for acme-worker: ```yaml
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: acme-worker
spec:
  pollingInterval: 30
  cooldownPeriod: 300
  triggers:
    - type: external
  minReplicaCount: 0
```

eng-deploy-bot: ALERT keda/acme-worker pulsed at 2024-06-12T19:11:05Z -> scale 0->4, pods reported NotReady states for ~40s (container logs: model init).

Jules (SE): I reproduced locally: fire 100 concurrent requests against a fresh deployment that has minReplicas=0. Results: queue builds; when KEDA scales new pods, readiness probe fails to transition before gateway timeout -> client sees 504. Root cause looks like combination of: 1) minReplicaCount 0, 2) long model init (no prewarm), 3) readiness probe too strict, 4) KEDA poll interval too coarse.

Jules (SE): Quick mitigations I tested successfully: set `minReplicaCount: 2`, lower readiness `initialDelaySeconds` to 5, and enable prewarm via annotation `redwood.io/prewarm: \"true\"` so the runtime warms KV cache on start. Also lowering KEDA pollingInterval to 10s reduced reaction time.

Izzy (oncall): For immediate mitigation: Marta, recommend routing Acme to a Dedicated pool for a short window (they agreed to try). Simultaneously, apply emergency change to ScaledObject: `minReplicaCount: 2` + `pollingInterval: 10`. We'll monitor and revert if noisy.

Marta (Support): On it — customer notified and agrees to dedicated routing for 2 hours while we stabilize. Opening support ticket #12345 and change request CR-7891.

Ravi (SRE): I'll apply scaledobject changes in staging first, then prod with a small maintenance window. Also adding an early-health hook in runtime to return healthy quickly while KV warms (grace window) so readiness doesn't block traffic unduly.

Marta (Support): After we switched Acme to dedicated + bumped minReplica, customer reported no 5xxs within 10 minutes and latency normalized. They're still asking for a postmortem and long-term mitigation.

Izzy (oncall): Action items: 1) Ravi: roll minReplica=2 + pollingInterval=10 for high-burst tenants; runbook for emergency change (ETA today). 2) Jules: produce prewarm annotation docs and a recommended readiness probe template for heavy models. 3) Marta: complete customer follow-up + escalate to AM. 4) Eng: consider autoscaler tuning (KEDA vs HPA hybrid) and default prewarm for certain model classes.

Ravi (SRE): I'll also add an alert to detect "scale-out but pods NotReady >30s" so we can auto-escalate next time.

Marta (Support): Logged follow-up meeting with Acme for tomorrow. Marking thread P1 -> resolved (customer stable) but keeping open until postmortem posted. :white_check_mark:

Izzy (oncall): Thanks team. Closing once postmortem and CR are complete.
